# Results — Study 778 (Chipotle-Scare)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**"buy the dip" on a Chipotle (CMG) food-safety scare**: the headline gaps the stock down
on fear, so a contrarian buys the panic and rides the recovery. This is a single-name
event study (shape D): the "event" is the day a specific scare became public, market-moving
news, and the trade is to buy CMG at that close and hold K sessions, measured as the
abnormal return (CMG − SPY). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30**. Fingerprint
`846252f83830` (CMG + SPY, one combined panel, adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return, split-adjusted) closes, `CMG` (Chipotle) + `SPY` (S&P 500), one combined panel: 3,393 rows, 2013-01-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 6 real Chipotle food-safety scares 2015→2018, anchored on the trading day each became public, market-moving news (CDC / state health departments / contemporaneous financial coverage — see [`references.md`](references.md)) |
| Excluded | the Aug-2015 Simi Valley, CA norovirus outbreak (234 sick) — Chipotle **did not disclose it at the time** (it surfaced only in a Dec-2015 / Jan-2016 lawsuit), so there is no contemporaneous market-moving date to anchor on. Honesty over sample size. |
| Events resolvable | all **6** of 6 scares have CMG+SPY coverage around the anchor |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return (CMG − SPY) across scare events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | **buy on public news, zero look-ahead**: the scare is already public when you act. Shock = [anchor−K → anchor]; rebound = [anchor → anchor+K]; net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for both legs |

**Two loud caveats, up front.** (1) **n = 6.** Four of the six scares are the *same* 2015
contamination crisis (Sept salmonella → Oct/Nov E. coli → the two December outbreaks), so
they are far from independent. (2) **Overlap.** The Dec-04 and Dec-08 2015 scares sit only
two sessions apart, so their post-windows are almost the same window. Any *t* below reads
as more precise than the true, dependence-adjusted evidence warrants.

## The shock — abnormal return, K sessions BEFORE the scare (CMG − SPY)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week shock (k=5) | 6 | **−3.877%** | **−3.451** | 0/6 = 0.0% [0.0%, 39.0%] |
| 1-month shock (k=21) | 6 | −9.806% | −2.640 | 1/6 = 16.7% [3.0%, 56.4%] |

The premise of the folklore is real: a Chipotle scare *is* a shock — CMG under-performs SPY
by ~3.9% in the week into the news (0 of 6 events were positive) and by ~9.8% over the
month. There is a genuine dip to buy.

## The rebound — abnormal return, K sessions AFTER the scare (the "buy the dip")

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month rebound (k=21) | 6 | **−9.329%** | **−2.355** | 1/6 = 16.7% [3.0%, 56.4%] |
| 1-quarter rebound (k=63) | 6 | −10.111% | −1.877 | 1/6 = 16.7% [3.0%, 56.4%] |

**The folklore is not merely absent — it is inverted.** "Buy the dip" would need a
*positive* rebound; instead CMG kept falling, under-performing SPY by another **−9.3% in
the month after** the scare and **−10.1% over the quarter**. Only 1 of 6 scares (the
Aug-2018 Powell, OH outbreak, +6.0%) rewarded the dip-buyer; the other five, all in the
prolonged 2015 crisis and the 2017 Virginia scare, kept sinking. This is a textbook
falling-knife: the scare is not a one-day repricing but the start of a slow bleed.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month rebound | right (the "buy the dip" claim) | −9.329% | +0.220% (3.725%) | **0.9968** |
| 1-month shock | left | −9.806% | +0.220% (3.725%) | 0.0022 |

The buy-the-dip rebound sits in the extreme **left** of the luck cloud — the right-tail
p = 0.997 means only ~0.3% of random one-month CMG windows were this *positive-or-better*,
i.e. the post-scare month was anomalously *bad*, the opposite of a rebound. But read it with
the n = 6 / one-episode caveat: the placebo treats the six events as independent, which they
are not.

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 1-month rebound *t*

Full-sample *t* = **−2.355**; across all 6 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[−4.027, −1.742]** — always negative. That looks robust, but it is *not* real
robustness: four of the six events are one autocorrelated 2015 episode, so dropping any
single event cannot break the dependence that drives the result.

## Tradability — net of costs (buy on public news, zero look-ahead)

| window | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month rebound | −9.329% (*t* −2.36) | −9.429% (*t* −2.38) | −9.529% (*t* −2.41) |
| 1-quarter rebound | −10.111% (*t* −1.88) | −10.211% (*t* −1.90) | −10.311% (*t* −1.91) |

The costed "buy the dip" long loses ~9–10% of abnormal return per event before you even
count borrow — it is a money-loser as stated. The *inverse* (short the scare and keep
shorting) "works" in-sample, but on 6 events across 11 years, dominated by one 2015 crisis,
with a hard-to-borrow, high-short-interest single name, it is a curiosity, not a strategy.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (bump = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = −0.29 (sd 0.76); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **0/20** seeds —
  the detector does not manufacture a rebound out of noise.
- **Planted rebound +3.0% (seed 784):** mean AR +2.77%, *t* = **+2.17**.
- **Planted rebound +6.0% (seed 784):** mean AR +5.77%, *t* = **+4.52** — a real rebound is
  recovered monotonically, so the *absence* of one on the real tape is informative, not a
  dead detector.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **Weak** | The *claimed* effect (a positive buy-the-dip rebound) is decisively **not** there — the rebound is negative (−9.3%, *t* = −2.36, right-tail p = 0.997), the reverse of the folklore. There is a suggestive post-scare *downdrift*, but it is fragile: n = 6, four of which are one autocorrelated 2015 crisis, with two December windows overlapping. Not indistinguishable from noise, but nowhere near robust. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank. "Buy the dip" loses ~9–10% per event net; the inverse short is a 6-event, one-episode, hard-to-borrow curiosity. No capacity, no independence, no edge you could run. |

**In one sentence:** the scare is a real dip, but you should *not* buy it — across six real
Chipotle food-safety scares CMG kept falling for a month (−9.3% vs SPY, *t* = −2.36) rather
than rebounding, so the contrarian reflex is a falling-knife, and even that "keep-shorting"
inverse is a fragile, un-bankable artifact of the 2015 crisis rather than a strategy.
